mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in RETAIL_REC mobility from its lowest point at t-1w to a higher value at t-0w suggests a reversal of the negative trend, indicating a sustained recovery that will lead to higher retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the mean of the last 28 days, indicating the t-0w rebound was an anomaly.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rebound in WORKPLACES mobility, increasing by more than 5 points week-on-week at t-0w, indicates a return to office work and associated weekday activities, which will spill over into increased retail and recreation footfall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increased by more than 5 points week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks despite the observed WORKPLACES rebound, or WORKPLACES declines again.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility increases while RESIDENTIAL mobility shows a slight decrease at t-0w, it signifies a collective shift away from home-based activities and towards external engagement, driving people towards retail and recreation options over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains stagnant even as WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The strong recovery in TRANSIT usage from its t-1w low, increasing by more than 5 points at t-0w, indicates increased public movement and confidence in using shared transportation, which will directly boost retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility increases but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next four weeks, or TRANSIT declines again.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained positive trend in PARKS mobility, consistently above baseline, indicates a general willingness of the population to leave their homes for leisure, which will eventually translate into increased retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks as people seek more diverse activities.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains positive or increases, but RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks, breaking the behavioral link.

mechanism_narrative: The relatively stable and less severe decline in GROCERY_PHARM mobility compared to RETAIL_REC suggests a resilient baseline level of essential out-of-home movement. This stability will prevent further significant drops in overall activity, leading to a slight recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as non-essential activities catch up.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines significantly, pulling RETAIL_REC further down, or RETAIL_REC fails to recover despite GROCERY_PHARM stability.

mechanism_narrative: The synchronized week-on-week rebound across RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES at t-0w strongly implies an easing of public health restrictions or a significant shift in public sentiment towards greater normalcy, which will sustain the recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: all three proxies increased week-on-week at t-0w
failure_condition: Despite the initial synchronized rebound, RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES all decline again in the next two weeks, indicating a false signal of policy easing.

mechanism_narrative: The consistently high and relatively stable RESIDENTIAL mobility, remaining above 5% baseline for two consecutive weeks, suggests a saturation point for staying at home has been reached. This will lead people to seek out-of-home activities, incrementally boosting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 5% baseline for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility continues to rise or RETAIL_REC declines in the next week, despite high residential activity, indicating no shift in behavior.
